messages:
tess: Drafting a rollout plan for Q2: 'adaptive-routing v3' (model-routing + path-priority). Need quick alignment on cohort slicing, telemetry gates, and fallback choreography. Thinking: tiered cohorts by SLA, region priming, and per-endpoint caps.
kevin: +1. can we avoid percent-based global slices? per-tenant buckets (gold/silver/free) give cleaner opt-outs. Also call out headroom for spikes.
maya: Agreed on tenant buckets. For regions: start with us-west1 -> eu-west1 -> ap-south1, 24h soak per region unless signal shows regression.
elaine: What telemetry gates do we want as hard stop? my vote: 99th latency increase > 20% OR error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute for 15m window. Also token-cost anomaly > 30% should throttle.
sam: +1 on latency/error. add qualitative sample checks—run a daily 1k synthetic prompt set and verify model-output similarity (BLEU/ROUGE-ish diff) before widening cohort.
tess: Good. Also propose automatic fallback policy: on gate trip, immediate switch to model-variant v3-small for affected cohort + notify ops and start rollback timer (30m) for manual review. If recovery within 10m, auto-reinstate.
kevin: How about burst protection? If we see 5s P99 spike but low error, maybe it's transient. Suggest keep a rolling 5m/15m policy: only escalate if both 5m and 15m exceed thresholds.
maya: Agree. And for dedicated customers (reserved capacity) we should honour their pinned variant unless they opt into early canaries. So by default exclude Dedicated from opt-in slices.
elaine: Ops checklist: make sure routing policies respect per-tenant rate limits and quota buckets. If a cohort hits token budget > 90% of daily allocation, shed to fallback model.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: adaptive-routing-v3 -> us-west1, cohort=gold-5pct, rollout_id=roll-1712600001. Monitoring hooks attached: latency/error/token_cost. :rocket:
nina: Quick config snippet for flags I put together: ```json
{
  "flag": "adaptive_routing_v3",
  "cohorts": [
    {"name":"gold","pct":5},
    {"name":"silver","pct":2},
    {"name":"free","pct":0.5}
  ],
  "regions":["us-west1","eu-west1","ap-south1"],
  "fallback":{"type":"model_variant","variant":"v3-small","auto_reinstate_after":"10m","manual_rollback_window":"30m"}
}
```
sam: Nice. Two asks: 1) Add a soft-kill switch for customer ops to pause cohort at tenant-level. 2) Telemetry contract needs a per-endpoint SLA baseline (we should store baselines from last 30d).
tess: Adding both. Also want a short playbook note: if synthetic diffs > threshold, pause rollout and run human review; if diffs minor but latency high, switch to v3-small and increase batching for affected shard.
kevin: What about A/B variant testing? We should run a small shadow A/B for output-quality vs cost: route identical traffic to v3 and v3-small in shadow for 48h and collect quality delta. Do not expose to users.
maya: Shadow A/B is good. Need to ensure privacy config (no logging of PII) during shadow.
elaine: Ops alerting: create a composite alert: (P99 latency up 20% OR error +0.5% OR synth-diff above threshold OR token-cost +30%) AND cohort traffic > 1rps => page oncall. Lower-severity alerts go to #product-telemetry.
tess: Final decision checklist for launch to next region: - Golden cohort stable 24h (no hard stop) - Shadow A/B collected for 48h with quality metrics - Dedicated customers either excluded or explicitly opted in - Playbook and kill-switch tested by oncall - Telemetry baselines uploaded to config store
nina: I'll update the flag payload and upload baseline scripts.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary quiesced after 4h for manual sample review (rollout_id=roll-1712600001). Samples saved to s3://redwood-rollouts/1712600001/samples.jsonl
sam: Thanks everyone — can folks ack when they've reviewed the playbook? I'll schedule a short dry-run tomorrow. :eyes:
kevin: Acked.
maya: Acked.
elaine: Acked.
tess: Thanks — moving to schedule dry-run and tagging ops for oncall drill.
